CORAM : R. D. DHANUKA AND  GAURI GODSE, JJ.
DATED : 19th APRIL, 2023 P.C. :-
1.
The matter is placed on board for speaking to the minutes of the judgment and order dated 11th April, 2023 passed by this Court only.
A preceipe dated 17th April 2023, filed by learned Advocate for the Petitioners points out the proposed corrections.
2. We shall first deal with the corrections suggested by the Petitioner and there is no objection from any of the Respondents to carry out those corrections/clarifications.

In paragraph 87, in 7 th line the words 'Section 32(2)' shall be corrected as 'Section 32(1)', in 10 th line of paragraph 87 words "sub-section (3)" shall be corrected as "
sub-section (4)", in last line of paragraph 87 figures "2019" shall be corrected as "2020", in 2nd line of paragraph 88, the words 'Section 32(2)' shall be corrected as 'Section 32(1)'.
In Second line of paragraph 88 'section 32(2)' shall be corrected as 'section 32(1)'.
In 13 th line of paragraph 88, 'Section 32(2)' shall be corrected as 'Section 32(1)'.
In paragraph 99, second line 'Respondent No.4' shall be corrected as 'Respondent Nos. 4 and 5'.

In paragraph 101(i), in second line figure mentioned as '49.349 hectare' shall be corrected as '46.361 hectare'.
In second line of paragraph 101(iv), the figure mentioned as '49.349 hectare' shall be corrected as '46.361 hectare'.

Learned counsel for the Respondent No.5 pointed out an inadvertent error in paragraph 7 of the judgment and submitted that there is no agreement dated 26 th December, 2020 executed between the Petitioner No.1 and Respondent No. 5 and seeks deletion of reference to execution of agreement dated 26 th December 2020.
Mr Narichania, learned Senior Advocate for the Petitioner, does not object this deletion.
He further states that it is not disputed that the Petitioner No.1 has transferred approximately 115 Acres of land to the Respondent No.5.

In paragraph 7, the following words "Petitioner No.1 and Respondent Nos. 5 thereafter entered into an Agreement dated 26 December, 2020 whereby the Petitioners transferred" shall be deleted and following words "Petitioners agreed to transfer" be inserted in its place.
In 3rd line of paragraph 100, figure mentioned as "49.349 hectors" shall be corrected as "46.361 hectors".
4. Petitioner is not pressing for the correction that the award shall be made within two months and not six weeks.
In so far as corrections suggested in paragraph 96, it is vehemently opposed by Mr Sakhare, learned Senior Counsel for Respondent No.1.
It is made clear that this Court has only recorded the contentions raised by the Applicant in Interim Application No. 2449 of 2023 in the said paragraph.
The This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 28/04/2023 905-cp-682-2022++.doc corrections suggested by the Petitioner thus cannot be accepted.

In Paragraph 101(iv), we have directed the Petitioner to hand over the possession of the balance land admeasuring 46.361 hectares to the Sub- Divisional Officer within two weeks from the date of order.

In so far as correction suggested in paragraph 101(ii) that there is no time prescribed for the Sub Divisional Officer to issue requisition to Respondent No.1 for deposit of the amount is concerned, Mr Narichania, learned Senior Counsel for the Petitioner submitted that though this Court has directed Respondent No.1 to deposit the amount that will be called by Sub Divisional Officer in respect of the said portion of land within two weeks from the date of such requisition,
inadvertently, there is no time prescribed for the Sub Divisional Officer to make such requisition for deposit of the amount in respect of portion of the land under acquisition.

He submitted that since this Court has already directed the Sub Divisional Officer to make an Award within six months,
which is inadvertently mentioned in paragraph 101(ii) shall be corrected.
Mr Sakhare, learned counsel for Respondent No.1, vehemently opposed this correction on the ground that it does not fall within the scope of Speaking to the Minutes of the Order.
He submitted that his client is ready and willing to deposit the amount before the award made by the Sub Divisional Officer.
He relied upon the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Akhil Bhartivarshiya Marwari Agarwal Jatiya Kosh v Brijlal Tibrewal 1.

sentences.text: He submitted that though this Court has given direction against Respondent No.1 to deposit the amount of compensation for acquisition of part of the land, there is no corresponding direction to the Competent Authority to call for such amount by issuing such requisition.

6. In so far as, objections raised by Mr Sakhare, learned Senior counsel for the Respondent No.1 is concerned, it is not in dispute that in paragraph 101(ii), this Court has directed Respondent No.1,
MIDC to deposit the amount that will be called for by Sub Divisional Officer in respect of said portion within a period of two weeks from the date of such requisition.

It is also not in dispute that this Court in Paragraph 101(vi) has directed the Petitioner to hand over the possession of balance portion of the land to the Sub Divisional Officer and the Sub-Divisional Officer in turn shall hand over possession of the balance portion of the land to the Respondent No.1-MIDC in accordance with Section 32(7) of the MID Act.
This Court has also directed the Competent Authority to make an Award from the date of said Order.
This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 28/04/2023 905-cp-682-2022++.doc 7.

While dictating the Order, this Court in paragraph 101(ii) directed Respondent No.1 to deposit the amount that will be called for by the Sub Divisional Officer in respect of portion of the said portion of land within two weeks from the date of such requisition, but inadvertently did not record through oversight the time limit for the Competent Authority to issue requisition for such deposit of amount from MIDC.

The apprehension of Mr Narichania, learned counsel for the Petitioner is right that if the possession has to be handed over within time prescribed and award to be made also within time prescribed and if the Sub Divisional Officer does not issue such requisition within six months, the Order could not be workable.

We agree that with submission made by learned counsel for the Petitioner that the time limit directing Sub Divisional Officer to issue requisition to the MIDC to deposit the amount has not been mentioned inadvertently and due to oversight while giving direction to MIDC to deposit the amount within two weeks from receipt of requisition from the Sub Divisional Officer.

There is no substance in the objections raised by Mr Sakhare, learned Senior Advocate for MIDC that correction suggested by Petitioner in paragraph 101(ii) does not fall within the purview of Speaking to the Minutes as clarified by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Akhil Bhartivarshiya Marwari Agarwal Jatiya Kosh (supra).

In paragraph 101(ii) add following sentence in the beginning of the paragraph "Sub-Divisional Officer shall issue requisition to the This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 28/04/2023 905-cp-682-2022++.doc Respondent No. 4 for depositing amount with respect to said portion of land within four weeks from today."

In the appearance of the learned counsel for the Petitioner in the order shall be corrected as Mr Rahul Narichania, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr Pranav Thackur, Advocate for the Petitioners.
8. Office is directed to correct the order and the corrected order be uploaded expeditiously.
Order dated 11 th April 2023, stand corrected accordingly.

(GAURI GODSE, J.) (R. D. DHANUKA, J.)
